values.note: Single site $27 a night, double $54. Cash or check in the fee envelopes at the entrance.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/park-creek-campground ('Single Site: $27 per night'; 'Double Site: $54 per night'; 'Fee envelopes and a collection box are provided near the entrance'; 'Please be prepared to pay with cash or check'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 13 gravel sites, maximum spur 35 ft but not every site takes that length; some sites are wider for larger RVs, and there is turnaround and parking space for trailers. Many sites sit beside the river under mature spruce and cottonwood.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/park-creek-campground ('13 gravel sites'; 'adequate turn around and parking space for trailers. Some sites are wider and can accommodate larger RVs'; 'Maximum spur length is 35 feet. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.'; 'Many sites are adjacent to the river'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Two vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water in season, central refuse bin (trash service Memorial Day - Labor Day); table and steel fire ring at each site, no firewood provided. Bear country.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/park-creek-campground ('2 vault type toilets, a centralized refuse bin and a developed drinking water system with hand pumps (in season)'; 'tables and steel fire rings (firewood is not provided)'; 'Trash service is provided by the concessionaire from Memorial Day to Labor Day'), read 2026-10-28

note: Rio Grande NF campground strung along the South Fork of the Rio Grande just off US-160, 7.8 miles west of South Fork and 9.5 miles below Wolf Creek Pass, ~8,500 ft; shady and secluded with heavy understory, but highway noise carries day and night. A handy overnight stop on US-160. --Claude
summary: FS page: confirmed 13 sites, $27 single, no hookups, FCFS only, two vault toilets, hand-pump water, 14-day limit. Added max 35 ft, season (Memorial Day - Labor Day weekend), senior/access 50%. Note trimmed of field facts; the old 'only a few sites take rigs over 30 ft; tight loop turnaround' is not in the FS text (it says there is adequate turnaround for trailers) and was dropped.

Waterfront vocabulary lead (stored riverfront, not changed): FS 'stretches along the banks of the south fork of the Rio Grande'; 'Many sites are adjacent to the river'. On Esri imagery the campground road runs along the river's west bank and the sites under the spruce/cottonwood canopy look within ~10-30 m of the water, but the South Fork here reads only ~15-20 m wide, under the ~30 m riverfront size rule - by size it is creekside. Pads are not visible under canopy and there are no per-site points, so which sites are on the bank can't be listed.
